verses.commentary: Come, let us return to the Lord. A liturgy of return, perhaps sarcastic. He has torn us but will heal. They recognize God's hand in judgment. He will bind up our wounds. Expectation of easy restoration.

After two days he will revive us. Quick recovery expected. On the third day he will restore us. Three days, then life. Early church fathers saw resurrection foreshadowed. That we may live in his presence. The goal of restoration.

Let us acknowledge the Lord. The right words. Let us press on to acknowledge him. Urgency. He will come to us like the winter rains. Certainty of God's arrival. But is this true repentance or ritualized expectation?
What can I do with you, Ephraim? God's lament. Your love is like morning mist. Beautiful but fleeting. Like early dew that disappears. No permanence. Their repentance evaporates.

Therefore I cut you in pieces with my prophets. Surgical judgment through prophetic words. I killed you with the words of my mouth. The word as weapon. My judgments flash like lightning. Swift, visible, unavoidable.
I desire mercy, not sacrifice. Jesus quotes this twice (Matthew 9:13, 12:7). Acknowledgment of God rather than burnt offerings. Relationship over ritual. The heart of prophetic religion.
As at Adam, they have broken the covenant. Whether the city Adam or the first man, the pattern is ancient. Covenant violation is not new. They were unfaithful to me there. Location of betrayal.
Gilead is a city of evildoers. The transjordan region. Stained with footprints of blood. Murder marks the streets. Violence made visible.
Bands of priests murder on the road to Shechem. Priestly gangs, highway robbers. They carry out wicked schemes. Religious officials as criminals.
I have seen a horrible thing in Israel. God as witness. Ephraim given to prostitution. The familiar charge. Israel is defiled. Ritual impurity from moral corruption.
A harvest is appointed for you, Judah. The southern kingdom not exempt. Whenever I would restore the fortunes of my people. Hope interrupted by continuing sin. Restoration delayed but not cancelled.
